name: Randall Glein
current_role: Co-founder & Partner, DFJ Growth; independent director, SpaceX (since Feb 2026)
profile: Randy Glein co-founded growth-stage VC firm DFJ Growth (joined 2002), investing in AI, space, deeptech and defense tech. A long-time SpaceX backer, he was a board observer from 2009 before joining SpaceX's board as an independent director in 2026; earlier he was CFO of FeedBurner (acquired by Google) and an executive at DIRECTV.
interesting_fact: He sat in on SpaceX board meetings as an observer for roughly 16 years (from 2009) before becoming a formal independent director ahead of SpaceX's IPO, with an expected seat on the audit committee.
deep_cut_fact: Before investing in rockets he built satellites' links himself: he began as a satellite communications engineer at GM Hughes Electronics and helped launch DIRECTV; he holds an EE degree from Univ. of Florida, an MS EE from USC Viterbi (1990) and a UCLA MBA, and is a near-scratch golfer.
notes: No personal contact published. Best route is via DFJ Growth (dfjgrowth.com; site blocks scripted access) or SpaceX media relations. Low public profile.

name: John M. Evans
current_role: Chief Executive Officer and director, Beam Therapeutics (since 2017)
profile: John Evans has led Beam Therapeutics, the Cambridge, MA base-editing gene-therapy company, since 2017, joining from ARCH Venture Partners as its launch CEO. Before that he was an early employee and SVP of corporate development and portfolio leadership at Agios, where he helped bring IDH inhibitors IDHIFA and TIBSOVO forward and co-led the Celgene alliance.
interesting_fact: Under Evans, Beam reported what it called the first-ever clinical genetic correction of a disease-causing mutation, with its in-vivo base editor BEAM-302 for alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency (2025).
deep_cut_fact: A gene-editing CEO with a humanities start: he earned a bachelor's in English with distinction from Yale before adding a Penn biotechnology master's and Wharton MBA; early career stops included MedImmune, McKinsey's pharma practice and Infinity Pharmaceuticals.
notes: Has said on podcasts 'I do not come from this field' — comfortable discussing the business side of biotech. Route via 1AB media contact.

name: Bill Wilson
current_role: Chief Executive Officer, Townsquare Media (NYSE: TSQ)
profile: Bill Wilson joined Townsquare Media in 2010 and rose from Chief Content & Digital Officer to co-CEO and then CEO, steering the local-radio owner into a 'digital-first' local media and marketing company. He previously spent nine years at AOL, ending as President of AOL Media, and began his career in the record business at Arista/BMG.
interesting_fact: Radio Ink named him its Radio Executive of the Year for 2021; he describes Townsquare's strategy as using 'radio as a Trojan horse to build a digital-first company.'
deep_cut_fact: He started as a product manager at Arista Records working on artists from the Notorious B.I.G. and Kenny G to Sarah McLachlan and Spiritualized, and later won a 2006 Emmy Award for AOL's Live 8 program; he graduated summa cum laude in economics from SUNY Stony Brook.
notes: Gives frequent trade-press interviews (Barrett Media, Radio Ink, Boyar Research Substack) — receptive to media; route via IR/Townsquare press office.

name: David S Wichmann
current_role: Independent director, Boston Scientific (since 2021) and Privia Health Group (since 2023); former CEO, UnitedHealth Group
profile: David Wichmann spent over two decades at UnitedHealth Group, rising from SVP of corporate development (1998) to CFO, president and then CEO from 2017 until early 2021, when Optum chief Andrew Witty succeeded him. He now serves as an independent director of medtech maker Boston Scientific and physician-enablement company Privia Health.
interesting_fact: He ran the largest US health insurer/health-services group as CEO (2017–2021) after earlier serving as its CFO and president — an accountant-turned-CEO of one of America's biggest companies by revenue.
deep_cut_fact: Before healthcare he was an auditor: an Illinois State University accounting graduate who made partner at Arthur Andersen, then moved to UnitedHealth in 1998 as SVP of corporate development.
notes: Low public profile since leaving UnitedHealth; no personal channels found. Approach only via board-company corporate secretary/press offices (Boston Scientific, Privia).

name: Brian Raduenz
current_role: Founder & Executive Chairman, AEVEX Aerospace (NYSE: AVEX); director, Karman Holdings; director nominee, Lyntris
profile: Brian Raduenz is a retired US Air Force lieutenant colonel who built AEVEX Aerospace, a defense-tech/drone and ISR company, from Merlin Global Services, serving as CEO 2014–Nov 2025 through multiple acquisitions before becoming executive chairman. He also sits on the boards of space/defense supplier Karman Holdings and defense connectivity company Lyntris.
interesting_fact: In the Air Force he oversaw early operational use of remotely piloted aircraft and spent his final decade leading government oversight of MQ-1 Predator and MQ-9 Reaper production and sustainment — then built a public drone/defense-tech company.
deep_cut_fact: An Air Force Academy electrical-engineering graduate (plus an AFIT MS EE), he was once named Air Force Outstanding Senior Engineer of the Year and served as Director of White House Presidential Contingency Programs under President George W. Bush.
notes: Bio sourced from Lyntris S-1/A (SEC). AEVEX site blocked scripted access; route via AEVEX Aerospace corporate communications. Web-search budget was exhausted during this lane, so contact lookup was limited.

name: Lynn M Bamford
current_role: Chair & CEO, Curtiss-Wright Corp. (becomes Executive Chair on Jan 1, 2027; Kevin Rayment succeeds her as CEO)
profile: Lynn Bamford has been with Curtiss-Wright for about 22 years, becoming President & CEO in January 2021 and Chair in May 2022. She has repositioned the aerospace & defense and commercial-nuclear supplier for growth, delivering record sales, orders and cash flow, returning $1.7B to shareholders and making several acquisitions; in Sept 2026 the company announced she will move to Executive Chair.
interesting_fact: She leads the direct corporate descendant of the Wright brothers' and Glenn Curtiss's aviation firms: Curtiss-Wright was formed in 1929 as the largest US aviation company and today supplies equipment for nuclear submarines and commercial nuclear power.
deep_cut_fact: An engineer by training: she holds a BS in electrical engineering from Penn State and an MS in electrical engineering from George Mason University, and has led Curtiss-Wright operations spanning more than 20 countries.

public_contacts.value: Jim Ryan, VP Investor Relations - Jim.Ryan@curtisswright.com

notes: Strong fit for an energy podcast (Curtiss-Wright is a major nuclear-power and naval-nuclear supplier). CEO transition on Jan 1, 2027 may free her schedule. Web-search budget ran out; deep cut limited to company bio.

name: Jon D. Kemp
current_role: Chief Executive Officer and director, Qnity Electronics (NYSE: Q)
profile: Jon Kemp is CEO of Qnity Electronics, the semiconductor and electronics-materials business separated from DuPont, supplying consumables for chip manufacturing plus materials for signal integrity, power and thermal management (AI data-center hardware). A 20+ year DuPont veteran, he previously ran DuPont's Electronics & Industrial and Electronics & Communications businesses and led Specialty Products strategy/M&A after the Dow-DuPont merger.
interesting_fact: Qnity's portfolio includes iconic DuPont-born materials brands such as Kapton polyimide film and Kalrez perfluoroelastomers, now sold alongside chip-fab consumables used in AI-era semiconductor manufacturing.
deep_cut_fact: He chairs the Board of Industry Leaders on SEMI's International Board of Directors (the global chip supply-chain association); he earned a BA in economics at the University of Utah and an MBA at UVA's Darden School, and early on was global business director for DuPont's Circuit & Packaging Materials.
notes: Good data-center/AI-hardware angle. Meg Miller (VP Global Communications) handles both IR and comms — best route.

name: Bruce D Wardinski
current_role: Chairman of the Board, DiamondRock Hospitality (from Apr 29, 2026); director, Accel Entertainment; former Chairman & CEO, Playa Hotels & Resorts
profile: Bruce Wardinski founded and led Playa Hotels & Resorts, an owner-operator of all-inclusive resorts in Mexico, the Dominican Republic and Jamaica, serving as chairman/CEO from 2017 until Hyatt acquired it in 2025 for about $2.6B including debt. A veteran hotel-REIT builder, he previously chaired Highland Hospitality and Crestline Capital and now chairs DiamondRock Hospitality.
interesting_fact: Hyatt's all-inclusive brands Hyatt Ziva and Hyatt Zilara were born from Hyatt's 2013 investment in Wardinski's Playa — a partnership that ended with Hyatt buying Playa outright in 2025.
deep_cut_fact: Accel's proxy credits him with leading 13 public companies across hotel REITs and operators — including chairing Crestline Capital (1998–2002) and Highland Hospitality (2003–2007); he holds a UVA commerce degree with honors and a Wharton MBA.
notes: Playa is now part of Hyatt (delisted), so no Playa IR channel. Best route is via DiamondRock Hospitality investor relations/corporate secretary. Web-search budget exhausted; contacts not further researched.

name: Sean Neville
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Catena Labs (AI-native financial institution); co-founder and board member, Circle
profile: Sean Neville co-founded Circle with Jeremy Allaire in 2013 and served as co-CEO until late 2019; Circle co-created the USDC stablecoin and is now public. In 2025 he co-founded Catena Labs with ex-Circle exec Matt Venables to build a regulated 'AI-native bank' letting AI agents transact under human-set policies; it raised an $18M seed and a $30M Series A (2026, Acrew and a16z crypto).
interesting_fact: In Sept 2026 the OCC granted Catena preliminary conditional approval for Catena Trust Bank, N.A. — a national trust bank built for AI agents and the businesses that deploy them.
deep_cut_fact: Asked what Catena would do with its $30M Series A, he answered: 'We are hiring humans' — at an 11-person company building banking for AI agents. He has argued that 'giving an agent a wallet is pretty easy compared with giving a business a governed way to trust it.'
notes: Very relevant for an AI/data-center-economy angle (agentic payments). Active in media (Fortune, Bloomberg). Personal social accounts not verified because web-search budget was exhausted.

name: Alex Tew
profile: British entrepreneur Alex Tew (b. 1984) became internet-famous at 21 for The Million Dollar Homepage (2005), which sold pixels as ads and earned over $1M in five months. After several web ventures he moved to San Francisco and co-founded Calm with Michael Acton Smith in 2012, building it into a leading meditation/sleep app valued around $2B, later expanding into Calm Health.
interesting_fact: The Million Dollar Homepage, created in 2005 to pay for university, sold a 1,000x1,000-pixel grid at $1 per pixel and grossed over $1 million within five months.
deep_cut_fact: Calm grew out of his 2011 side project 'Do Nothing for 2 Minutes' (built with developer Ben Dowling, later Calm's first CTO) — a page that reset the timer if you touched your mouse; he'd started meditating at age 14 in Wiltshire.
notes: Calm has had a separate CEO (David Ko) since 2022; Tew's exact current title unverified. Personal social accounts not verified (web-search budget exhausted). Meditation-at-14 detail is from BBC Worklife profile: https://www.bbc.com/worklife/article/20160914-the-man-behind-the-million-dollar-homepage

name: Eoghan McCabe
current_role: Chairman & CEO, Fin (formerly Intercom), which agreed in June 2026 to be acquired by Salesforce
profile: Irish entrepreneur Eoghan McCabe co-founded Intercom in 2011 with Des Traynor, Ciaran Lee and David Barrett, building it into a customer-messaging platform. After returning as CEO he pivoted the company around its Fin AI customer-service agent, renamed it Fin in May 2026, and in June 2026 agreed a sale to Salesforce for about $3.6B.
interesting_fact: In March 2026 the company raised $250M in venture debt rather than equity to fund its AI agent, with McCabe saying he chose debt to avoid diluting shareholders — three months before agreeing the ~$3.6B Salesforce deal.
deep_cut_fact: Before Intercom, McCabe and his co-founders ran a Dublin design consultancy called Contrast, which built a bug-tracking tool named Exceptional; selling Exceptional to Rackspace in 2011 provided the money to start Intercom.
notes: Outspoken on X/Twitter (Irish Times has covered his posting); personal handle not re-verified because web-search budget ran out. Pending Salesforce acquisition may affect availability.

name: Eric Setton
current_role: Co-founder of Tango (TangoME, Inc.); current role not confirmed
profile: Eric Setton co-founded Tango with Uri Raz in Mountain View in September 2009, as one of the first free mobile video-calling/messaging apps on 3G; it raised a $280M round in 2014 from Alibaba, Jerry Yang and others and passed 400M registered users by 2018. Tango later pivoted (2017) into live-streaming with a virtual-gifting economy; Raz is CEO.
interesting_fact: Tango's March 2014 financing brought in $280 million from Alibaba, Yahoo co-founder Jerry Yang and other investors — one of the largest consumer-messaging rounds of its era.
notes: Low public profile; current title not verified. Likely (but not confirmed as same person) the Eric Setton who co-authored the Stanford/Springer book 'Peer-to-Peer Video Streaming' (2007) with Bernd Girod — verify before using. Tango's live-streaming business has faced content/scam controversies (app removed from Apple App Store in 2026), so tread carefully. Web-search budget exhausted.

name: Dhaval Shah
current_role: Co-founder, PharmEasy (API Holdings); current executive role not verified
profile: Dr. Dhaval Shah co-founded Mumbai-based e-pharmacy PharmEasy in 2015 with Dharmil Sheth, alongside API Holdings co-founders Siddharth Shah, Hardik Dedhia and Harsh Parekh. PharmEasy grew into India's largest online pharmacy, buying rival Medlife and a 66.1% stake in listed diagnostics chain Thyrocare in 2021, reaching a ~$5.6B valuation before a later down-round reset.
interesting_fact: In 2021 PharmEasy's parent did the rare deal of a unicorn buying a listed company — acquiring 66.1% of Thyrocare from founder Dr A. Velumani in a ₹4,546 crore transaction.
